title: As a lurker here for a while, I'm curious as to why so many here have the same recurring mallworld dreams?
content: I've never had a mall world dream but they sound interesting, I wish I could have one. I've just been wondering if people have it because of maybe a nostalgia for malls? Or fond memories of malls? The way the mallworld I see commonly described is like a city but inside a whole building but with mall aesthetics and neon/futuristic designs. The closest thing that comes to mind for me are the megablocks or megabuildings from the scifi subgenre of cyberpunk (Judge Dredd, Cyberpunk 2077, Bladerunner etc). The other thing I think of is that it sounds like the original idea of what the mall was supposed to be. Malls were meant to be a solution to American suburbs, for it to be a place where people can go to the park, go to stores, also have their apartment, movie theater, recreational activities, also schools all in one (look up Victor Gruen). The weirdest detail I've noticed about mallworld dreamers is that their dreams synchronize. If one person had an earthquake in their dream, someone else on here will comment and say they felt it. In fact many even report the exact same locations popping up. Even the bathrooms are all described the same way. How is it possible that people from different parts of the world with different experiences and culture can dream about the same place that doesn't actually exist? Is it proof of this reality being a simulation or dream? Is this a modern phenomenon or did ancient people ever have similar dreams? Why do only some people have them and others don't?
